sections.h2: Why do Flint sales hinge on condition and clear title?
sections.html:
Flint homes sell for far less than homes elsewhere in Michigan, so a seller's outcome depends on repair costs, liens and ownership history more than on the asking price. Flint is the Genesee County seat, about 66 miles northwest of Detroit on the Flint River, and the Census Bureau estimated 79,306 residents on July 1, 2025.

A Flint owner has three paths: an agent listing, a direct sale to a neighbor or investor, or a buyer who pays cash and takes the house untouched. The sections below set each path against the city's rental ordinance, its water billing rule, county tax foreclosure and the figures behind local values.

sections.h2: How has Flint's history shaped its housing today?
sections.html:
Fur trader Jacob Smith founded a trading post here in 1819, the village incorporated in 1855, and lumber and carriage building turned into automobile manufacturing. Buick moved to Flint, Chevrolet built its first plant here, and General Motors was founded in the city in 1908. Local GM employment peaked near 80,000 in 1978 and fell below 8,000 by 2010.

Population followed the jobs down. It reached about 197,000 in 1960 and measured 81,252 in the 2020 Census. The housing stock was built for that larger workforce, so a seller here is often marketing an older house to a smaller pool of buyers than the city once had.

  • Older houses can carry repair items such as roofs, wiring and plumbing that a buyer's inspector will list.
  • The Land Bank holds vacant lots and houses, so some occupied blocks sit beside empty parcels.
  • Tax foreclosure has shaped ownership here, so parcel history deserves a look before you sign anything.
  • The city lived through a lead-in-water emergency from 2014 to 2019, and Wikipedia reports a new water source plus copper service pipes at nearly every home since, so buyers may ask what work was done at your address.

sections.h2: How low are Flint home values, and who owns the houses?
sections.html:
QuickFacts describes a city where renters nearly match owners and where the middle owner-occupied house is valued at $53,500.

At $53,500, a new roof or furnace can swallow a large part of an owner's equity. That arithmetic leads many Flint owners to weigh a quick sale of the house as it stands against the delay and expense of bringing it to retail condition.

sections.h2: Which Flint neighborhoods and landmarks matter to buyers?
sections.html:
Flint's neighborhoods are grouped around downtown, which is centered on Saginaw Street south of the river. Carriage Town and the Grand Traverse Street District hold preserved Victorian houses just west of downtown. East of I-475, Central Park and Fairfield Village sit between the University of Michigan-Flint and Mott Community College. East Village and the College Cultural Neighborhood on the east side are described as more stable, and the west side includes Mott Park and the Woodcroft Estates.

Public schools are run by Flint Community Schools, which operates ten elementary schools, one middle school and Flint Southwestern Academy. Catholic and charter schools also serve the city. Kettering University, UM-Flint and Mott Community College are all in or beside the city's core.

sections.h2: What are Flint's rental rules, and do they affect a sale?
sections.html:
They do if the house has tenants. Flint's rental ordinance requires rental properties to be registered with the city and certified after an inspection. A December 2023 city memo put the single-family registration at a one-time $250 and the inspection at $225 every three years, and it said tenants make up nearly half of Flint households. Landlords must provide heat from October 1 through March 31.

The same memo explains a water rule that surprises owners: the city prefers water accounts in the owner's name, and unpaid water bills become a lien that can be added to the property tax bill. Before selling a rental, make sure the water account is paid and call the Building and Safety Inspections Division at 810-766-7284 to learn where the certification stands. Fees change, so request the current schedule.

sections.h2: How does Genesee County tax foreclosure affect Flint sellers?
sections.html:
A delinquent tax bill can move a house into county tax foreclosure, and that is a real risk for owners of inherited or vacant property. The Genesee County Land Bank takes in properties through the tax foreclosure process: houses that go unsold at the public auction and are not claimed by the state or a local government are transferred from the County Treasurer to the Land Bank at the end of each calendar year.

Owners in the city can check parcel ownership through the city's property lookup, and a parcel listed under Genesee County LRC Inc or the Genesee County Treasurer is held by the Land Bank. For a seller, the lesson is simple: pay or arrange the back taxes before the foreclosure clock runs out, because a sale closed on time keeps the equity that an auction would not.

  • Get the exact tax balance from the county treasurer before signing a purchase contract.
  • Unpaid water bills can sit on the tax roll as well.
  • Ask the title company to pull liens early so surprises do not delay closing.

sections.h2: What does the Michigan transfer tax cost on a Flint house?
sections.html:
Two Michigan transfer taxes apply: 55 cents for the county plus $3.75 for the state on every $500 of price, per MCL 207.504 and 207.525. The seller bears them, and payment goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered (MCL 207.523).

A sale at Flint's middle value of $53,500 would owe about $460, and the settlement statement will give the real figure. The buyer then notifies the city assessor within 45 days so that taxable value can reset the next year (MCL 211.27a).

sections.h2: When does an as-is sale beat a listing in Flint?
sections.html:
A sound house on a stable block can do well with an agent, provided the buyer's appraisal supports the contract price. When repairs would cost more than they add, or a lien, code order or tenant dispute clouds the deal, selling the house untouched removes most of the friction.

  • An agent listing suits a move-in-ready house when you can wait through loan approval.
  • An as-is buyer suits a house whose repair quotes outrun its likely sale price.
  • A neighbor suits an empty lot beside their home, a logic the Land Bank applies when it sells side lots.

Ask for proof of funds, read the closing date clause, and compare offers by what you keep after liens and costs.

faqs.q: Can unpaid property taxes be settled out of a Flint sale?
faqs.a: Usually yes, if closing happens before the county finishes foreclosure. The title agent subtracts the balance from your proceeds, and the Genesee County Treasurer can confirm the payoff and the foreclosure timeline.

faqs.q: Do unpaid Flint water bills follow the house?
faqs.a: They can. City rules let delinquent water charges become a lien added to the property tax bill, so a title agent will usually want the account paid before closing.

faqs.q: What does Flint expect of a landlord?
faqs.a: Rentals must be registered and certified after an inspection, repeated every three years, and landlords must supply heat from October 1 through March 31. Request the current fee schedule from Building and Safety Inspections.

faqs.q: What would Michigan transfer tax come to at Flint's typical home value?
faqs.a: About $460 on $53,500, combining 55 cents per $500 for the county with $3.75 per $500 for the state. Your settlement statement shows the exact amount.

faqs.q: What is the Genesee County Land Bank?
faqs.a: A county entity that receives tax-foreclosed properties that fail to sell at auction. It sells houses and lots, offers side lots to neighboring owners and demolishes dangerous structures as funding allows.
